A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same A-MEM study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C can be matched reliably using text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original LoCoMo evaluations across six foundation models, component ablations, retrieval-parameter experiments, and memory-embedding analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main evaluations and supplementary results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Note construction, link generation, memory evolution, and retrieval remain unchanged in Section 3, including equations (1)–(10) and the corresponding prompts in Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same LoCoMo coverage: single-hop, multi-hop, temporal, open-domain, and adversarial questions. No dataset, task, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain the same evaluated comparators: LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, and MemGPT. The ablation configurations in Table 2 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The six foundation models, evaluation metrics, embedding model, retrieval procedures, and model/category-specific k settings remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B, including Table 5.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 2, k sensitivity analysis in Figure 3, memory visualizations in Figures 4–5, and question-answering example in Appendix C.4 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting practice. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings, plotted findings, and example outputs are unchanged. For instance, A-MEM with GPT-4o-mini retains multi-hop F1/BLEU-1 scores of 45.85/36.67 in Table 1.

T1.justification: The memory representations and mathematical procedures in Section 3 and the metric formulas in Appendix B.1 are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about autonomous memory organization, memory evolution, reasoning performance, and efficiency.

C2.justification: The interpretations of interconnected memories, retrieval tradeoffs, and embedding clustering are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same qualifications concerning underlying LLM capabilities and the text-only implementation.

D1.justification: v1 provides WujiangXu/AgenticMemory as the source-code repository. v4 identifies it as evaluation code and adds agiresearch/A-mem for the memory-system implementation. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, and prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: No cited research works are added or removed. Section 2 and Appendix A preserve the same comparisons with earlier memory systems and agentic RAG approaches.

P1.justification: Author affiliations and the abstract’s code-availability sentence are edited. The scientific prose, terminology, and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Front-page and heading spacing changes reflow the main text and references, including moving the Introduction opening into the right column. Figure and table designs are unchanged; appendix pages 13–20 render identically.

improvement.justification: v4 improves code-access guidance by distinguishing the evaluation repository from the memory-system implementation and providing a separate link for the latter. This offers a limited benefit for reproduction and reuse; the scientific evidence, explanations, and limitations remain unchanged.
